- **self**: Grid trading and market making viability (4/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Queue position and cancel speed decide who captures the maker edge. In Albers et al. (large near-side queue, small opposite-side queue), the 1-second markout excluding rebate averaged -0.058 bp for front-of-queue fills and -0.775 bp for back-of-queue fills; when the queue was small, position mattered little. Multicoin says makers that cancel stale quotes first, segment flow or hedge fast can quote tighter, and credits Hyperliquid's rule that cancels execute before new taker orders for much of its liquidity. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2502.18625 · keywords: Grid trading and market making viability · also: https://multicoin.capital/2026/02/17/adverse-selection-rules-everything-around-me

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] A grid bot is a range and mean-reversion bet, and a sustained trend breaks it. In a downtrend it keeps buying, builds a growing long with negative unrealized PnL, and holds the full position once price falls below the lower bound. In an uptrend it sells out and sits flat, missing the rally. Bitsgap's replay shows the cost of a range that does not fit the market: 7 of its 8 liquidated futures replays were spot bots already losing 25% to 90%. Hummingbot's own Avellaneda-Stoikov guide gives the same inventory example for a symmetrical strategy in a BTC-USDT downtrend. (medium confidence) — https://dev.to/joe_hans_6c082d6c1caf189f/i-ran-a-gateio-btc-grid-bot-for-6-months-real-returns-and-3-fatal-mistakes-2i1p · keywords: Grid trading and market making viability · also: https://bitsgap.com/blog/spot-vs-futures-grid-bot-what-backtests-show, https://hummingbot.org/blog/guide-to-the-avellaneda--stoikov-strategy/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Avellaneda-Stoikov (A&S) is the inventory-risk market-making model that Hummingbot implements. The original model assumes a finite trading session, and Wang et al. note that A&S-style models assume the maker knows the stochastic dynamics of the state variables. Hummingbot adapts the model to 24/7 markets with a user-set session length. Because the paper gives no way to calculate risk aversion (gamma) or order-book depth (kappa), Hummingbot's easy mode estimates both from spread limits. Neither Hummingbot A&S page presents backtests, fees or adverse-selection analysis. (medium confidence) — https://hummingbot.org/blog/guide-to-the-avellaneda--stoikov-strategy/ · keywords: Grid trading and market making viability · also: https://hummingbot.org/blog/technical-deep-dive-into-the-avellaneda--stoikov-strategy/, https://arxiv.org/html/2508.16588

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] One practitioner's grid guardrails (anecdotal, single source): block new orders when free balance falls under a threshold (about 40 USDT for roughly 10 concurrent grids), warn at margin ratio below 10% and hard-pause below 5%, add an external drawdown stop, use wide ranges rather than tight ones, and keep leverage at 2x or lower. Tight ranges raised fee bleed and left the bot idle outside the range for two weeks after a 3,000 USD daily move. (low confidence) — https://dev.to/joe_hans_6c082d6c1caf189f/i-ran-a-gateio-btc-grid-bot-for-6-months-real-returns-and-3-fatal-mistakes-2i1p · keywords: Grid trading and market making viability
